clue.text: Taking family out of India, faculty man offering no Option 28

parts.note: wit is a mental faculty, as in 'have your wits about you'

indicators.note: the faculty man is taking something in, holding it inside his name

parts.note: Thomas Hobson, the Cambridge carrier whose customers took the horse nearest the door or none: Hobson's choice

indicators.note: taking something out of a word leaves it without that piece, so one letter here is dropped

parts.note: kin are one's relatives
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A university lecturer turns down an option, having taken the family out of India.
explanation.walkthrough: Hobson's choice, taking what is offered or nothing, is no real choice at all. The definition is a cross-reference to the answer at 28-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British idioms meaning 'and more besides', added to stress that something is so to an even greater degree.

clue.text: Foul stuff on Instagram keeps going up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the phrase keeps the answer inside it, held within its run of letters

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of stuff, all of on and the start of Instagram

explanation.surface: Objectionable material posted on Instagram keeps appearing.
explanation.walkthrough: An in-off is a snooker or billiards term: the cue ball goes into a pocket after striking another ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Potting the cue ball off another ball is a penalty in snooker, so an in-off is a type of foul shot.

clue.text: Vegetation secure in this area

indicators.note: one word is placed in another, so it sits within that word's letters

parts.note: here means in this place
to bag something is to secure or obtain it

explanation.surface: A note that the plant life is safe within this patch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is herbaceous growth such as grass and other plants used for grazing, i.e. vegetation collectively.

clue.text: One's established in one's territory

indicators.note: the answer lies in the words that follow, spelt out across them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of one's into the start of territory

explanation.surface: Someone describes how a creature makes itself at home on its own patch.
explanation.definitionFit: A nester is one that has made a nest, i.e. one who has settled down and become established somewhere.

clue.text: 1960s dance girl blocks one bishop in error

indicators.note: a girl who blocks someone stands in their place, so she takes over one letter's spot

parts.note: a boo-boo is a silly mistake
gal is an informal word for a girl
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop; one of the two in the error is removed

explanation.surface: A dancing girl gets in a clergyman's way by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: GAL takes the place of the second B in BOOBOO.
explanation.definitionFit: The boogaloo is a dance that was popular in the mid-to-late 1960s, related to the twist and funk styles.

clue.text: Exuberantly cavort around East Ham

indicators.note: the word for the compass point is put inside, with the other letters around it
doing something exuberantly means wildly and unrestrainedly, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Someone leaps about with high spirits in East Ham, a district of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East Ham' reads as the London district, but East gives E and Ham is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform in an exaggerated, theatrical way, which is exactly what overacting means.

clue.text: Select old woman consumed by pain in toe to have foot injected

indicators.note: whatever is consumed by something ends up inside it
an injection goes inside, so this piece is put within another

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one thing set in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp pain
O is the abbreviation for old
FT is the abbreviation for foot
her is a pronoun standing for a woman

explanation.surface: A gruesome account of an elderly woman with toe pain who needs a foot injection.
explanation.walkthrough: Three nested insertions: the foot goes into the old woman, she goes into the pain, and the pain goes into the toe from the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Select as an adjective means choice or of the best quality, as top-of-the-range goods are.

clue.text: See 15
Cutting-edge picture house generous person has adopted

indicators.note: one who has adopted something has taken it in, so it goes inside

parts.note: a soft heart is a kind, generous person
the Tate is a London art gallery, a house for pictures

explanation.surface: A philanthropist has taken over a modern cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture house' suggests a cinema, but here the pictures are paintings: the Tate gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting-edge and state-of-the-art are both adjectives for the newest, most advanced technology or design.

clue.text: Work at reversing the Telegraph team's reputation

indicators.note: reversing means running backwards, so the letters are read right to left

parts.note: to do something is to work at it
the newspaper's own staff would say 'our'

explanation.surface: A complaint that the newspaper's staff are working to undo their good name.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue appeared in the Telegraph, so its team speaks of itself as 'our'.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour is used for standing or repute, as in being in good odour or bad odour with someone.

clue.text: A chinwag with street singer

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
a means one
a chinwag is an informal chat

explanation.surface: A gossip with a busker on the pavement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Street singer' looks like a busker, but the street gives ST and singer is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The stonechat is a small songbird of heath and scrub, named for its call like two stones knocked together.

clue.text: Artist withdrew to rear of studio?

definitions.text: Artist withdrew to rear of studio?

indicators.note: sent to the rear, the artist's abbreviation goes at the back, after the other piece

parts.note: 'off came' is an inverted way of saying something came off, i.e. was withdrawn
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter retreated to the back of the studio.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a performer who retreats to the back of a TV studio is out of shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Off camera means out of the camera's view, which is where someone at the back of a studio would be.

clue.text: Lead off dog you'll notice lower value

indicators.note: with its lead off, the word loses its leading letter

parts.note: the hound at 20-across, which sits lower down the grid

explanation.surface: Taking the leash off a dog appears to reduce its worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a dog's leash, but it is the first letter. The dog is the answer to 20-across, below in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something of worth, a thing that has value to its owner.

clue.text: Panel up to entering races around island?

indicators.note: something entering another word goes inside it

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) motorcycle races are run on roads around the Isle of Man
being up to a task means being able to do it

explanation.surface: A committee is capable of joining the racing around an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a flat slab or panel, e.g. of stone or wood, often bearing an inscription.

clue.text: Add-on features mysterious isle oddly below Shetlands

indicators.note: something mysterious is puzzling and obscure, so the letters are jumbled out of recognition

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: oddly means taking only the odd-numbered letters, first, third and so on

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Extras on offer at some enigmatic island north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells and whistles is an idiom for attractive extra features added to a product beyond its basic function.

clue.text: Left potatoes in Taj Mahal office pro tem

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship
aloo is the Hindi word for potato, on the menu in a curry house named Taj Mahal

explanation.surface: Leftover potatoes at an Indian restaurant are being kept in a temporary office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' is an old euphemism for a lavatory. A Portaloo is a British brand of portable toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Portaloo is a temporary toilet, and pro tem means for the time being, so it is a stopgap lavatory.

clue.text: Liking to reverse the order of song-writing?

indicators.note: the two pieces are joined the other way round from the way the clue gives them

parts.note: to pen is to write
a chant is a simple song

explanation.surface: A songwriter's fondness for writing the words before the music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song-writing' reads as one word for composing, but it splits into two pieces whose order is then swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a strong taste or inclination for something, so it is a liking.

clue.text: Figures view potting shed from behind

indicators.note: seen from behind, the letters are taken from the back, right to left
potting something puts it in a pot, so this word is set inside another

parts.note: to view is to see
to spill is to shed, as in shedding a load

explanation.surface: A gardener's view of the potting shed from the back of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potting shed' reads as a garden hut, but potting is a container signal acting on shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellipses are oval geometric figures, plural of ellipse.

clue.text: Give lots of notice new, greener, power is in the ascendancy

indicators.note: rising up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
greener means less experienced, i.e. rawer
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A political warning that new, more environmental power is on the rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greener' suggests environmental politics, but here it means more inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: To prewarn is to warn in advance, giving someone plenty of notice before something happens.

clue.text: Hound prepared to track what's left of boar so far

indicators.note: tracking means following behind, so this piece comes after the others
the left end of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the leftmost letter
as, in the sense 'as yet', means up to now, so far
set means ready or prepared

explanation.surface: A hunting dog is ready to follow the trail of what remains of a boar.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset is a short-legged, long-eared breed of hound bred for tracking by scent.

clue.text: Nonplussed when nutmegged by Crete's defender

indicators.note: in football, to nutmeg a player is to pass the ball between their legs, so one word goes through the middle of the other

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
Talos was the bronze giant of Greek myth who guarded Crete

explanation.surface: A footballer is baffled at having the ball slipped through his legs by a Cretan defender.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nonplussed means being so surprised and confused that you are unsure how to react: at a loss.

clue.text: No TV after editing, every bit cut

indicators.note: editing reworks and rearranges text, so the remaining letters are rearranged
no means without, so these letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A programme is ruined because every scene was cut in the editing suite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like the editor's work on a TV show; it is a cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Rib-eye is a cut of beef steak taken from the rib section.

clue.text: Is getting porter perhaps to secure passageway

indicators.note: securing something holds it fast, so one word is held inside another

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hotel porter is being sent to lock up a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a doorman; it is a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between rows of seats, as in a church, plane or theatre.

clue.text: Attentive to one's beard, perhaps set for posh dinner?

parts.note: a beard grows on the chin
aware means alert or attentive

explanation.surface: Someone grooming their beard to get ready for a smart dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The beard is only an example of what grows on the body part needed, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinaware is porcelain tableware, the fine dinner service laid out for a formal meal.

clue.text: Man should carry a cross, it's generally accepted

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece that carries sits underneath, holding the rest up on top

parts.note: taken as written
an X is a cross
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A religious maxim that a man should bear his cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is capitalised to start the sentence and hides the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement taken as self-evidently true, a principle that is generally accepted without proof.

clue.text: Mate stops drinking, finally, in fantastic pub

indicators.note: a stopper sits in a gap, so the friend is plugged into the middle
finally means at the end, so only the last letter is used

parts.note: its last letter
taken as written
a pal is a mate, a friend
ace is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A friend finally gives up drinking in a fabulous bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stops' looks like quitting the drink, but it means the mate plugs a gap. A gin palace is a gaudy Victorian pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin palace was a showy, brightly decorated Victorian public house, and the term is still used for a flashy pub.

clue.text: Twig the contents of knitted underwear

indicators.note: contents are what lies inside, so the outer letters are discarded

parts.note: hosiery is knitted stockings and socks; drop its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A pun on twig meaning to realise what is inside someone's knitwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twig' looks like the verb to realise; it is a noun, a willow shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a willow whose long flexible shoots or twigs are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Quite a few more meet hands-on doctors

indicators.note: doctors used as a verb means tampers with or alters, so the letters are falsified into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: More people get to meet hands-on doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' looks like a noun, the medics being met; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: And then some is an idiom meaning that and a good deal more besides, i.e. considerably more.
